###Part A: Importing and inspecting a CSV.

#A1 Import employees.csv into a data frame  named emp_df using read.csv() with stringAsFactors = FALSE.
```{r}
emp_df <- read.csv("employees.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
emp_df
```

#A2 Display the structure, the first 5 rows, and summary of emp_df
```{r}

str(emp_df)
head(emp_df, 5)
summary(emp_df)
```

#A3 print the number of rows and the number of colunms of emp_df,and the class of every column 
```{r}


nrow(emp_df)
ncol(emp_df)
sapply(emp_df, class)
```

#A4 Print the mean salary, the maximum age, and the number of employees in each department using table()
```{r}

mean(emp_df$salary)
max(emp_df$age)
table(emp_df$department)

```

###B Create Data Frames

#B1 Create a data frame new_hires with the same column  names  as emp_df and these three employees
```{r}

new_hires <- data.frame(
  emp_id = c(21, 22, 23),
  name = c("Uma", "Victor", "Wen"),
  department = c("HR", "IT", "Sales"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "F"),
  age = c(28, 37, 33),
  salary = c(45000, 83000, 60000),
  years_service = c(2, 9, 6),
  rating = c(3, 4, 5)
)


new_hires

```

#B2 use rbind() to append new_hires to emp_df, saving  the result  as emp.all. print the dimensions of  emp.all
```{r}


emp_all <- rbind(emp_df, new_hires)
dim(emp_all)
```

#B3 add a column  bonus to emp.all equal  to 5% of salary, rounded  to the nearest  whole number.
```{r}


emp_all$bonus <- round(emp_all$salary * 0.05)
print(emp_all)

```
###C Subsetting 

#C1 Extract  the3 first  5 rows  and only  the columns  name and  salary, using  numeric  or name  indexing.
```{r}

emp_all[1:5, c("name", "salary")]
```

#C2 Using logical  subsetting, select all  employees  with salary ,using  numeric or name  indexing.
```{r}
 
emp_all[emp_all$salary > 70000, ]
```

#C3 using subset function, select employees  in the "IT" 
```{r}

subset(emp_all,
       department == "IT" & years_service >= 5,
       select = c(name, years_service, salary))

```

#C4 Use which () to print the row numbers of employees older than 50, then print  their names.
```{r}

which(emp_all$age > 50)
emp_all$name[which(emp_all$age > 50)]



```

#C5 remove  the column  emp_id and bonus using negative indexing. do not  overwrite emp_all; print the first 3 rows of the results.
```{r}

emp_removed <- emp_all[, -which(names(emp_all) %in% c("emp_id", "bonus"))]
head(emp_removed, 3)


```

#C6 (2) Using logical indexing, print the salary of the employee whose name is "Mia"
```{r}

emp_all$salary[emp_all$name == "Mia"]




```
###D Factors

#D1 Convert department and sex in emp_all to factors with factor(). Print levels() of each. 
```{r}
emp_all$department <- factor(emp_all$department)

# Convert sex into a factor
emp_all$sex <- factor(emp_all$sex)

# Print the department levels
levels(emp_all$department)

# Print the sex levels
levels(emp_all$sex)
```

#D2 Use table() to count employees per department, and make a two-way table of department by 'sex.
```{r}
table(emp_all$department)
```

#D3 Create an ordered factor rating_level from rating using factor() with levels = 1:5 and
#labels = c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Very Good", "Excellent"). Add it to emp_all and print
#table(emp_all$rating_level)
```{r}

emp_all$rating_level <- factor(
  emp_all$rating,
  levels = 1:5,
  labels = c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Very Good", "Excellent"),
  ordered = TRUE
)


table(emp_all$rating_level)

```

#D4 Using a for loop over levels(emp_all$department) and logical subsetting, print the mean salary of
#each department, rounded to the nearest whole number.
```{r}
# D4: Calculate and print the mean salary of each department using a for loop and logical subsetting
for (dept in levels(emp_all$department)) {
  mean_sal <- round(mean(emp_all$salary[emp_all$department == dept]))
  print(paste(dept, ":", mean_sal))
}

```
###EConditional Statements

#E1 Using nested ifelse(), add a column salary_band to emp_all: "High" if salary >= 70000, "Medium"
#if salary >= 50000 (and below 70000), otherwise "Low". Print table(emp_all$salary_band) ..
```{r}
emp_all$salary_band <- ifelse(
  emp_all$salary >= 70000, "High",
  ifelse(emp_all$salary >= 50000, "Medium", "Low")
)


table(emp_all$salary_band)

```

#e2# Categorize employees based on years of service
```{r}
emp_all$level <- ifelse(
  emp_all$years_service >= 8, "Senior", "Junior"
)


table(emp_all$level)

```
#e3# Create a function to determine the raise percentage
```{r}
# E3: Define the raise_pct function
raise_pct <- function(rating) {
  if (rating == 5) {
    return(0.10)
  } else if (rating == 4) {
    return(0.07)
  } else if (rating == 3) {
    return(0.04)
  } else {
    return(0)
  }
}


emp_all$raise <- sapply(emp_all$rating, raise_pct)


emp_all$new_salary <- round(emp_all$salary * (1 + emp_all$raise))


head(emp_all[, c("name", "rating", "raise", "new_salary")], 5)
```
#E4 Using an if / else statement (not ifelse()), compute total <- sum(emp_all$new_salary) and print
#"Budget OK" if the total is below 1,600,000, otherwise print "Over budget". Also print the total ..
```{r}

total <- sum(emp_all$new_salary)


print(paste("Total:", total))


if (total < 1600000) {
  print("Budget OK")
} else {
  print("Over budget")
}
```

###Part E: Conditional Statements

#F1 Use sort() to print the 5 highest salary values in decreasing order, and the first 5 employee name values
#in alphabetical order.
```{r}

sort(emp_all$salary, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5]


sort(emp_all$name)[1:5]
```

#F2 Use order() to sort emp_all by salary in descending order and print the name, department and
#salary of the top 5. Save the sorted data frame as 'by_salary.

```{r}

by_salary <- emp_all[order(emp_all$salary, decreasing = TRUE), ]


head(by_salary[, c("name", "department", "salary")], 5)
```
